settings.question: Do I need true summer tires in Calgary, or are all-seasons enough?
settings.answer: Most Calgary drivers don't need dedicated summer-only tires. The summer season here (May–September) is short, and a quality all-season touring tire handles dry and wet conditions just fine. Dedicated summer tires make sense if you have a performance sedan, sports coupe, or EV where you want maximum dry/wet grip in the warm months and you already run dedicated winters for the cold half.

settings.question: When should I install summer tires?
settings.answer: If you're running a true summer/UHP set, install in late April once overnight lows stay above 7°C and pull them off by late October. Summer compound rubber goes hard and brittle below 7°C and gives away grip dangerously fast — never leave them on through a Calgary cold snap.

settings.question: How long do summer tires last in Calgary?
settings.answer: Summer UHP tires typically last 4–6 seasons of warm-weather use (about 30,000–50,000 km on a sport sedan). They wear faster than all-season touring tires because the softer compound that gives them grip also rubs off faster. Touring all-seasons used as a warm-season set last 5–7 years — much longer mileage.

settings.question: Can I use summer tires year-round in Calgary?
settings.answer: No — and this isn't a soft no. Summer tire rubber compounds harden below 7°C and lose meaningful grip. By -10°C they're functionally unsafe. Calgary sees -25°C regularly. Run them through one winter and you'll destroy the tread AND lose vehicle control on the first cold morning. Always pair summer tires with a dedicated winter set.

settings.question: How much do summer tires cost in Calgary?
settings.answer: Premium UHP summer tires (Bridgestone Potenza Sport, Michelin Pilot Sport 5) run $280–$450 per tire depending on size. Touring all-seasons used as warm-weather tires (Michelin Defender 2, Continental TrueContact Tour) run $180–$320 per tire. Price-matched to any written Calgary quote on the same model and size.

settings.heading: What summer tires actually do in Calgary
settings.intro:
Summer tires are optimized for warm pavement — soft rubber compounds and shallow tread blocks that maximize contact patch on dry and wet roads. True UHP summer tires are a step beyond touring all-seasons in dry-handling and wet-braking. Touring all-seasons used as warm-weather tires are the more common Calgary setup — long tread life, quiet ride, predictable grip.

For Calgary specifically, the calculus is short — only about 5–6 months of warm weather to spread the cost across. That makes touring all-seasons the more pragmatic choice for most drivers. UHP summer makes sense when the performance gain matters to you.
settings.outro: If you want one tire all year that's also 3PMSF-rated for winter, see the all-weather tires Calgary guide. If you'd rather run dedicated winters Nov–Mar and summer/all-season for the warm half, that's the cleaner setup.
